To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cytokine signal transducing factor STAT3 is transiently activated in axotomised neurons of the medial septum, and that the same factor is also activated in reactive astrocytes in the septum after fimbria-fornix transection.
the transcription factor signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) is transiently activated in axotomised septohippocal neurons and in reactive astrocytes of lesioned brain regions.
cytokine signaling is transiently activated in axotomised neurons and in reactive astrocytes following a lesion of the septal projection neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activation of the STAT3 signaling pathway in neurons and reactive astroglia after central nervous system injury.
the question of whether and to what extent neurotrophic factors, in particular the family of gp 130-associated cytokines, are involved in the response to axonal injury in the adult CNS.
the activation of STAT3 signaling after CNS injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

STAT3 activation in neurons after axotomy may not be mediated by gp130-associated cytokine signaling, whereas the STAT3 activation in reactive astrocytes is most likely mediated by gp130 associated cytokines.
STAT3 is a key molecule in the neuroprotective signaling of the cytokines.

the activation of STAT3 signaling is not a prerequisite for lesion-induced cytokine expression and that the activation of cytokine receptors in the lesioned brain does not necessarily lead to activation of STAT3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the STAT3 activation after CNS lesion is mediated by gp130-associated cytokine signaling and that the activation of STAT3 in neurons and astrocytes is independent of the cytokine ligands CNTF and LIF.
STAT3 is transiently activated by FFT in axotomised septal neurons and reactive astroglia.
cytokine-mediated STAT3 signaling is involved in the regulation of both neuroprotection and reactive gliosis after CNS injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
STAT3 is activated in neurons and astrocytes after CNS lesions.
cytokines have a role in the CNS that goes beyond their role as neurotrophic factors.
the gp130-associated cytokine system is activated after central nervous lesions.
